newsitem.title: USA: AirTouch, US West deal erases uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: AirTouch, US West deal erases uncertainty.

text.p: AirTouch Communications Inc's revised $4.5 billion plan to acquire U S West Media Group's cellular phone operations has erased much investor uncertainty about the transaction, analysts said.

AirTouch and U S West agreed to merge their cellular operations in 1994 in a complex, three-step deal. The final value of that transaction was never clear to investors because it was based on an appraisal of U S West's cellular operation.
On Friday, AirTouch and U S West agreed to a simpler method where AirTouch would pay about $2.2 billion in stock and assume $2.2 billion of U S West's debt.

"This transaction eliminates much of the uncertainty surrounding the previous agreement," said Kevin Roe, analyst at investment bank ABN AMRO Chicago Corp. "With this, they spell out the terms of the deal and the timing."

Investors seemed to like the terms of the new deal. Shares of AirTouch, based in San Francisco, rose one to 24-1/2 on New York Stock Exchange trading of one million shares. U S West shares rose 3/8 to 17-5/8.
"It's a good move to put the two companies together," said Charles DiSanza, analyst at investment bank Gerard Klauer Mattison in New York.
"They've been operating together for a while and already the economies of scale have helped the U S West properties get substanially more profitable."
The combined company would offer coverage from the West Coast to the Mississippi River, serving 1.9 million customers in 20 states.

"The markets that U S West has -- Denver, Seattle, Salt Lake City -- are some the fastest growing in the country," said Mark Lowenstein, director of wireless research at market researcher Yankee Group in Boston.
The companies expect to close the transaction by the end of the year, but warned it could be called off if Congress approves the Morris Trust legislation, introduced on Thursday.

The legislation would close loopholes that let companies sell pieces of their operations without paying taxes. If the legislation passes and if it is applied to U S West's sale of cellular properties to AirTouch, the companies would call off the deal, executives from the companies said.
